exercises.name: Lying Neck Curls (Weighted)

source_english.description: Weighted lying neck curls add a light plate to a small supported neck-flexion movement.
instructions: Lie on your back with the head supported and place a light plate securely on the forehead with both hands.
Tuck the chin slightly and keep the shoulders relaxed.
Nod the chin toward the chest through a small controlled range.
Lower the head slowly while keeping the plate stable.
form_cues: Keep the plate centered and supported.
Move slowly from a neutral neck.
common_mistakes: Pressing the plate into the forehead.
source_english.safety_note: Only use a light, secure plate and stop at any neck discomfort or instability.

exercises.name: Meadows Rows (Barbell)

source_english.description: A Meadows row uses the free end of an anchored barbell and a staggered stance to pull one arm toward the ribs.
instructions: Anchor one end of the barbell and stand beside the free end in a staggered stance.
Hinge at the hips, brace the trunk, and grasp the sleeve with the nearer hand.
Pull the bar toward the lower ribs while keeping the hips and spine steady.
Lower the bar under control, complete the side, and switch arms.
form_cues: Keep the bar close to the body.
source_english.safety_note: Secure the landmine anchor and keep the free end clear of your feet and knees.

exercises.name: Overhead Plate Raise

source_english.description: An overhead plate raise lifts a weight plate from chest height to overhead with both hands while the ribs stay stacked.
instructions: Stand with feet stable and hold the plate at chest height with both hands.

Raise the plate overhead without leaning back.
Lower it slowly to chest height and repeat.

source_english.safety_note: Use a light plate and keep a firm two-handed grip throughout the raise.

exercises.name: Preacher Curl (Barbell)

source_english.description: Preacher Curl (Barbell) supports the upper arms on a preacher pad while the weight curls toward the shoulders and lowers fully.
instructions: Sit on a preacher bench with your upper arms resting on the pad and your chest against the support.
Grasp the barbell with an underhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Keeping your upper arms stationary, exhale and curl the barbell up towards your shoulders.
Pause for a moment at the top, squeezing your biceps.
Inhale and slowly lower the barbell back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
form_cues: Use a steady squeeze at the top.
source_english.safety_note: Choose a load that keeps the wrists and elbows aligned without momentum.

exercises.name: Rack Pull

source_english.description: Starting with the barbell elevated around knee height, extend the hips and knees to stand tall, then lower to the rack.
instructions: Set up a barbell on a rack at knee height.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly outwards.
Bend at the hips and knees to lower yourself down and grip the barbell with an overhand grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and lift the barbell by extending your hips and knees, pulling your shoulders back and squeezing your glutes at the top.
Lower the barbell back down to the starting position by bending at the hips and knees.

exercises.name: Russian Twist (Weighted)

source_english.description: Russian Twist (Weighted) rotates the trunk from side to side while the seated torso stays braced and balanced.
instructions: Sit on the ground with your knees bent and your feet flat on the floor.
Hold a weight or medicine ball with both hands in front of your chest.
Lean back slightly, keeping your back straight and your core engaged.
Slowly twist your torso to the right, bringing the weight or medicine ball towards the floor on your right side.
Pause for a moment, then twist your torso to the left, bringing the weight or medicine ball towards the floor on your left side.
Continue alternating sides for the desired number of repetitions.
form_cues: Rotate the ribcage side to side while the pelvis stays balanced.
source_english.safety_note: Use a comfortable range and stop if control or alignment deteriorates.
